decision: Always serialize the workspace basePath on every terminal WS URL, not only when a project is selected
rationale: buildAIWsUrl() set the basePath param inside the if(options.projectName) block although createAISession() always threads the value in; a no-project /ai-coding session therefore sent mount=~/jarvis with no basePath, the server fell back to its hardcoded ~/prj default, and every AI session died with close 1008 Path not allowed. buildWsUrl()'s claude branch had the identical omission
alternatives: Fix only the server default (leaves the client sending incomplete state and the same trap for any other consumer); change the server default to derive from HOST_WORKSPACE_PATH only (does not help host mode and still relies on an implicit convention)

decision: Add tildeToHostWorkspace() and map ~/<basename(HOST_WORKSPACE_PATH)> onto the host workspace root in the WS mount resolver, independent of the client-supplied basePath
rationale: In container mode expandPath() resolves ~ against the CONTAINER home (/home/node), so a tilde mount that does not match basePath produced /home/node/jarvis — a container path used as a HOST bind-mount source that translatePath() cannot map into /workspace, so the #186 confinement check could only ever reject it. The hardcoded ~/prj default guarantees this on any deployment whose workspace basename differs, and a client-only fix leaves every stale browser tab broken
alternatives: Relax the #186 confinement check (rejected: the check is correct, the path handed to it was wrong); default basePathParam to the workspace basename (rejected: same implicit convention, but silently mis-resolves any other tilde path)

decision: tildeToHostWorkspace() takes the workspace root as a parameter instead of reading HOST_WORKSPACE_PATH or homedir()
rationale: Keeps the helper pure so its tests cannot collapse the host and container home namespaces into one value — the mocking failure mode that previously hid a /workspace-vs-~/prj mismatch in this same code. The test suite pins a workspace root outside any home directory for the same reason
alternatives: Keep the helper module-local in connection-handler.ts reading the HOST_WORKSPACE_PATH const (rejected: only testable by importing the whole WS handler with its PTY/docker/recorder dependencies, and env-const timing forces resetModules gymnastics)

decision: Recreate the live galway daax container on a locally built fix image, preserving the existing single-container topology rather than switching to the split web/terminal deploy compose
rationale: The running container was created outside compose (no compose labels) and runs both planes; the repo deploy/docker-compose.yml is now the split F3 topology. Changing topology while fixing an outage would confound the fix with an unrelated migration. The previous container is retained stopped as daax-prev-fixbasepath and the prior image tagged ghcr.io/daax-dev/daax-web:rollback-20260817 for rollback
alternatives: Wait for a merge to main and the GHCR publish (rejected: leaves the site broken and only humans may merge); docker compose -p daax -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build (rejected: silently changes the deployed topology)

decision: Start the pre-existing daax-postgres container, which had sat in Created state since 2026-07-27
rationale: /api/health returned db:false and the app container had 20746 consecutive failing health checks. The data directory on daax_daax-pg-data already contained an initialized PG18 cluster, so starting it skips initdb and is reversible with docker stop; health now returns ok/db:true. Unrelated to the WS bug — Traefik does not gate on health, so the outage was reached independently
alternatives: Leave it and only report (rejected: the app was running degraded with its catalog/releases/audit store unreachable); recreate via compose up (rejected: would recreate sibling services and risk a wider change during an outage fix)
